description: Two production builds as successive releases in event mode. The webpack path injects chunk ids and the release into every client and server chunk before hashing; the Turbopack path uses native debug ids and uploads from runAfterProductionCompile. A Pages API route captures two exceptions server-side through an externalized posthog-node; both must resolve to their source lines and carry the release. On the Turbopack path the release reaches the bundled posthog-js through env, but not an externalized posthog-node: no runtime module sets _posthogReleaseId there, so server exceptions resolve but carry no release while browser exceptions carry it. Before @posthog/nextjs-config 1.11.4 the release id was injected into every chunk after hashing, so the webpack runtime kept its URL while its chunk map changed (posthog-js#5332): a browser served the previous release's runtime reported the previous release, and every other chunk was renamed each deploy.
